reasoning: ComputeTempDeformKokkos::restore_bias_all_kk (line 148-159) does 'if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->restore_bias_all();' while its mirror image ComputeTempDeformKokkos::remove_bias_all_kk (line 123-134) correctly does 'temperature->remove_bias_all_kk();'. Compute declares both as virtuals (src/compute.h:153-159). Every KOKKOS temperature compute implements the non-_kk entry point as the _kk one plus a host sync — e.g. ComputeTempCOMKokkos<DeviceType>::restore_bias_all (src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_com_kokkos.cpp:223-227) is '{ restore_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK); }' — so the wrong call adds a full device-to-host copy of v on every invocation. No correctness impact (sync(Host) only refreshes the host mirror and leaves the device copy valid), purely wasted bandwidth on the inner thermostat loop. The same asymmetry exists in src/KOKKOS/fix_nh_kokkos.cpp lines 579 and 734 ('temperature->restore_bias_all()' next to 'temperature->remove_bias_all_kk()' at 558/716); fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:371, fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:159, fix_temp_csvr_kokkos.cpp:159 and fix_temp_rescale_kokkos.cpp:162 all get it right.

reasoning: ComputeTempDeformKokkos<DeviceType>::remove_deform_bias_all_kk (lines 173-198) syncs and binds the DeviceType views ('atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK|V_MASK|MASK_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();'), then calls 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal);' before launching Kokkos::parallel_for on RangePolicy<DeviceType,...>. DomainKokkos::x2lamda(int n) (src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:672-687) is not templated: outside the detached_atom_x() fallback it does 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view_device(); Kokkos::parallel_for(RangePolicy<LMPDeviceType,TagDomain_x2lamda>(0,n),*this); atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK);'. So it converts only the device copy and marks the DEVICE copy modified, leaving the host mirror holding Cartesian coordinates. The file instantiates ComputeTempDeformKokkos<LMPHostType> under '#ifdef LMP_KOKKOS_GPU', and in that build LMPHostType != LMPDeviceType so the two x mirrors are distinct memory. The TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias kernel then reads the stale Cartesian host x and computes vbiasall from Cartesian rather than lamda coordinates. On a CPU-only Kokkos build the mirrors alias and the bug is invisible, which is why it survives testing.
fix: Do not mutate atom->x at all: follow the CPU style and compute lamda per atom inside the kernel. Cache domain->h_inv and domain->boxlo in KK_FLOAT members before the launch and inline 'lamda = h_inv * (x - boxlo)' (the TagDomain_x2lamda body) in TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias, then delete the domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal)/lamda2x(nlocal) pair. That fixes F0091 at the same time. If the round trip is kept instead, x2lamda/lamda2x must be made DeviceType-aware (or the compute must sync/modify X in the correct space around them).

The CPU style never touches atom->x: ComputeTempDeform::remove_bias_all (src/compute_temp_deform.cpp:307-317) declares 'double lamda[3];' and calls 'domain->x2lamda(atom->x[i], lamda);' into that local, as do compute_scalar/compute_vector/remove_bias/restore_bias (lines 256, 275, 313, 354). The KOKKOS round trip therefore perturbs atom->x by the round-off of two matrix transforms — amplified here because k_x holds KK_FLOAT, which is single precision in a mixed/float build — and additionally costs two extra full-array device passes plus X_MASK sync traffic per call. Confirmed as described; impact is small in a double build, hence low.
fix: Same edit as F0078: compute the lamda coordinate inside TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias from cached h_inv/boxlo instead of converting atom->x in place, and remove the x2lamda/lamda2x pair. This makes the KOKKOS style bit-comparable to the CPU one and removes the host/device divergence of F0078.
